A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MAC-Flow research. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices support comparison, including the additional experiments in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, timing measurements, offline-to-online experiments and ablations in Section 5 and Appendix H.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds controlled coordination experiments in Section 4.3 and Appendices H.4–H.7.

M1.justification: The joint flow model, IGM-based critics, distillation and value objectives, and decentralized one-step inference remain unchanged. Algorithms 1–2 and the implementation descriptions retain the same procedure.

E1.justification: The four original benchmarks remain, but v2 substantially extends diagnostic coverage with a partially observed landmark-covering task, larger teams, an imbalanced binary coordination game, and a continuous XOR task with anti-aligned optimal actions. These introduce task conditions beyond the retained benchmark evaluations.

E2.justification: Table 2 removes BC and adds MADiff across the existing MA-MuJoCo and MPE comparisons. MADiff already appeared in the discrete-control comparison, whose comparator set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: The added experiments introduce substantial new evaluation protocols: tracking distillation loss, mutual information, Wasserstein discrepancy and value bounds; scaling landmark teams to 40 agents; and sweeping joint-action mixture weights from 0 to 1. H.4 uses 50 trajectories, 1,000 training iterations and batch size 64. Existing benchmark protocols are retained.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component ablations, v2 adds empirical checks of the theoretical bounds, agent-scaling analysis, a controlled comparison of value-guided distillation against imitation, an XOR failure test, and a distribution-mixture sensitivity study. These substantially expand analysis of mechanisms and failure conditions.

E5.justification: Both versions specify six seeds and mean plus or minus two standard deviations for Tables 1–2, with tolerance intervals for existing learning curves. v2 introduces no additional stated repeated-run, uncertainty-estimation or significance-testing procedure for the new toy experiments.

E6.justification: Table 2 replaces BC results with MADiff results while retaining the other methods' scores. For example, newly reported MADiff scores 4711.4 ±213.6 on HalfCheetah-Expert, above MAC-Flow's unchanged 4650.0 ±271.6. Figures 3 and 13–16 add substantial findings concerning value bounds, scaling, value-guided action selection and failure to reproduce XOR modes.

T1.justification: The existing definitions, propositions, complexity analysis and Appendix D proofs are unchanged. H.6 adds an XOR counterexample argument concerning factorization, and H.7 introduces an explicit joint-distribution mixture for its interaction analysis. These are limited mathematical additions rather than new performance guarantees.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same two-stage MAC-Flow contribution and performance–efficiency claims, including approximately 14.5-fold faster inference. The new diagnostic evidence does not redefine these central claims.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly distinguishes bounded performance degradation under assumptions from perfect preservation of global optimality. Sections 4.3 and H.4–H.7 add substantive interpretations of dependency preservation, scaling, value guidance and nonfactorizable failure cases, including a new interpretation of distribution mixtures as interaction strength.

D1.justification: v2 documents observation and reward construction for the new toy tasks, the mixture-generation rule, and H.4's trajectory count, training iterations and batch size. Existing architecture, hardware, benchmark hyperparameters and repository-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning in Section 2 and Appendix B are unchanged. Removing an unresolved citation marker and updating bibliography backreferences do not add or remove identifiable prior work.

P1.justification: v2 inserts Section 4.3 and Appendices H.4–H.7, renumbers the algorithm summary, adds a short experimental overview, repairs broken references and removes an empty limitations heading. Existing prose and the overall narrative structure are largely retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds five substantive multipanel figures: Figure 3 and Figures 13–16. Table 2 changes comparator columns and abbreviates dataset labels, while the main tables and plots are rearranged. The original figure content is retained.

improvement.justification: Adding MADiff to continuous-control comparisons and documenting factorization failures improve scrutiny of v1's claims. However, H.7 calls an anti-correlated two-mode distribution nearly independent and interprets its mixture sweep as increasing dependence, although both endpoint distributions are nonfactorizable. This undermines an important new interpretation. The useful additional evidence and newly introduced conceptual problems leave the net quality effect uncertain.
